big_sets.why: Sets covering a quarter to three quarters of the ranked list. The permutation draws then reject often -- sampling 300 distinct indices out of 400 by rejection takes far more than 300 draws -- so the RNG consumption pattern is completely different from the small-set case, and a port that samples without reproducing the rejection loop diverges only here.

coarse_permutation.why: -p 20, so permutation p values land on a 1/20 grid: 30 pathways share 14 distinct p values across 37 tied pairs, which the FDR step-down pass then collapses to 7 distinct FDR values. That is where a port's FDR can differ while every p agrees, because the step-down takes a running minimum over tied runs rather than adjusting each value independently. ES still breaks almost every tie, so the row ordering here stays defined -- the cases with genuinely unordered pairs are tie_extreme and big_sets.

custom_seed.why: --seed 20260311. The seed reached the helper only in PR #52; before that it reseeded from the clock. This case fails if a port accepts the argument and ignores it, which is the quiet way to get that wrong.

degenerate_sets.why: A set covering the whole ranked list (n <= nf, the division getgseascore_fast guards), a set overlapping it not at all (empty index), a set of duplicates (Size and the scored count come apart), and three singletons (num == 1, so p_gsea reduces to the percentile itself). Real GMT files contain all four.

gmt_blank_line.why: A blank line in the GMT makes parsegmt store a pathway whose name is the empty string. main() then finds PM.count(args.pname) > 0 -- because args.pname defaults to "" -- and takes the single-pathway branch, so it reports that one empty pathway and silently skips every real one, exiting 0. Confirmed against the binary: a 2-set file plus one blank line produces a single junk row. The port must ignore blank lines.

gmt_description_with_spaces.why: GMT is a tab-delimited format whose second column is free-text description, but parsegmt reads the line with `ss >> ssf` and treats every token after the second as a gene name. So a description containing spaces has its second and later words silently added to the gene set. Mostly they match nothing and only inflate Size -- but gene symbols occur in prose descriptions constantly ("regulation of TP53 activity"), and a word that does match is added to the set and changes its result. Confirmed against the binary: giving a two-gene set the description "response to G01" moved ES from 5.55e-17 to 0.396226 and p from 0.9025 to 0, because G01 is the top-ranked gene. The port must read the GMT as tab-delimited.

gmt_missing_final_newline.why: parsegmt loops `while(true){getline; if(eof) break;}`. On a file whose last line has no newline, that getline sets eofbit while returning the line, so the loop breaks before storing it: the last gene set is silently dropped. Confirmed against the binary -- it reports one pathway fewer and says nothing. The port must keep the set.

gmt_trailing_whitespace.why: `while(ss.good())` runs one iteration past the last token when a line ends in whitespace, and a failed `>>` into a std::string leaves it empty rather than untouched, so a phantom empty gene name joins the set. It never matches anything, but it inflates the Size column -- the number users read as the gene-set size -- by one. Confirmed against the binary. The port must not count it.

many_pathways.why: 150 sets over 2000 genes at -p 1000: the scale at which the permutation stream is consumed millions of times and in strict pathway-name order. A port that parallelises over pathways, or iterates them in file order rather than lexicographic order, produces plausible numbers that agree with nothing.

no_header.why: Without -H the header row is parsed as a gene. atof() of a column label is 0.0, so a phantom gene joins the ranking and shifts the line count every other score is divided by. Reproducing this matters because -H is a flag a user can forget.

production_default.why: Exactly what `mageck pathway` runs for negative selection: -s -H -c 2 -p 1000. Every other case is a variation on this one, so if this fails nothing else is worth reading.

production_positive.why: The second call `mageck pathway` makes, on the positive-selection column (-c 8). Same code path as the first, but it proves the column index is honoured rather than hardcoded -- a port reading a fixed column would pass production_default and fail here.

rank_missing_final_newline.why: The same loop in parserankfile, and worse: dropping the last gene also lowers the line count that every gene's score is divided by, so one missing newline perturbs the whole ranking rather than just losing a row. The port must keep the gene.

rank_only.why: -c 0: the other branch of parserankfile entirely. The score comes from a gene's line number, the genes are not re-sorted, and the normalisation counts from 1 instead of 0. No existing test reaches this branch.

reverse.why: -e reverses the gene *names* after scoring but leaves the score vector alone (calculategsea.cpp:237-239), so it is not the symmetry its name suggests: gene i keeps position i's score. A port that reverses both agrees on nothing here.

single_pathway.why: -n names one pathway, which takes the branch in main() rather than testallgseas, prints Ranking as 1 and runs no FDR pass at all. Also the only path where the permutation stream is consumed by one pathway instead of all of them in name order.

tie_extreme.why: Scores rounded to one decimal, which collapses 400 genes onto about ten distinct values. Degenerate on purpose: it turns a rare tie-breaking disagreement into one that shows up everywhere.

tie_heavy.why: Scores rounded to two decimals, so genes tie by the dozen. Ties are resolved inside parserankfile by sorting (score, name) pairs, which means the gene order -- and therefore every score -- depends on a name comparison a port could easily omit.

tiny_sets.why: Every set has between one and three genes, so num - gindex is always small and BetaNoncentralCdf is evaluated at the edge of its parameter range rather than in the comfortable middle.

unsorted.why: Without -s, testallgseas takes a different output branch that writes the permutation p into the FDR column and leaves Ranking at 0. Not what `mageck pathway` passes, but it is the documented default of the helper's own CLI.

tolerances.es_is_platform_dependent: The ES column is not reproducible to the last bit, which is why atol_es exists. getgseascore_fast computes decvalue*(ni-i) + sumincval, which clang contracts into a fused multiply-add at -O3 wherever FMA is in the baseline instruction set (it is on the arm64 these were recorded on; it is not on baseline x86-64). Rebuilding the same source with -ffp-contract=off changes three of these goldens by 2.776e-17 and 5.551e-17, in gene sets whose score cancels to zero. Read the platform block above before concluding that a mismatch in that digit means anything.
tolerances.note: every number is written through ostream << with default flags, i.e. six significant digits, so the file itself bounds how closely two implementations can be compared. p_permutation is required to agree exactly: the generator is seeded and its consumption order fully determined, so there is no Monte Carlo noise to allow for.
